chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave who was freed and married, and bore a daughter to her first master, whether he could marry his daughter. He said: She is forbidden to him, and she is his slave daughter; the free woman is the same in this regard. Then he recited: 'Your step-daughters who are in your households'.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of his freed female slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of marrying the daughter of one's freed female slave (rabīb) applies equally whether she was originally a slave or free, establishing the principle of 'al-umm wa al-bintā' wa al-ukht' (mother, daughter, sister) consistency in mahram relationships. This ruling is derived from Surah An-Nisa, verse 23, which explicitly mentions 'rabā'ibukum' (your step-daughters) in the context of those in your household, a category that Shia jurisprudence extends to include daughters of freed slaves due to the established bond of upbringing and ownership. The hadith underscores the legal equivalence of free and slave women in forming these familial prohibitions, a key nuance in Usuli fiqh.
